chunks: A group of scholars informed me, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Quluwayh and Abi Ghalib al-Zarari (and others), from Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kulayni, from Ishaq ibn Yaqub, who said:

I asked Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari, may Allah have mercy on him, to convey to me a letter in which questions that were difficult for me were posed. The Tawqi' (reply) came in the hand of our Master, the Master of the Era (peace be upon him):

As for what you asked about regarding those who deny me from among our family and our cousins, know that there is no kinship between Allah (Exalted and Mighty) and anyone. Whoever denies me is not from me, and his path is the path of the son of Nuh (peace be upon him).
As for the path of my uncle Ja'far and his sons, it is the path of the brothers of Yusuf (peace be upon him).
As for Al-Fuqaa' (barley wine), its drinking is forbidden, and there is no harm in Al-Shalmaa' (turnip extract).

As for your wealth, we do not accept it except to purify you. So whoever wishes, let him send it; and whoever wishes, let him withhold it. What Allah has given us is better than what He has given you.
As for the Reappearance (of the Imam), it is with Allah (Exalted and Mighty). The time-fixers have lied.
As for the saying of those who claim that Husayn (peace be upon him) was not slain, it is disbelief, denial, and deviation.
As for the events that occur, refer to the narrators of our Hadith, for they are my proof upon you, and I am Allah's proof upon them.
As for Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari, may Allah be pleased with him and his father before him, he is my trustworthy one, and his writing is my writing.
As for Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar al-Ahwazi, Allah will soon reform his heart and remove his doubt.
As for what you sent us, we accept only that which is pure and clean. And the price of the singing girl is forbidden.
As for Muhammad ibn Shazan ibn Naeem, he is a man from our Shia, the People of the House.

As for Abul-Khattab Muhammad ibn (Abi) Zainab al-Ajda', he is cursed and his companions are cursed. Do not sit with those who hold their belief, for I am aloof from them, and my forefathers (peace be upon them) are aloof from them.
As for those who are clad in our wealth, whoever deems a portion of it lawful and consumes it, he is consuming the Fire.
As for Khums, it has been permitted for our Shia and they are in ease regarding it until the time of our Reappearance, so that their offspring may be pure and not impure.

As for the regret of a people who doubted in the religion of Allah regarding what they sent us, we have returned to whoever asked for return, and we have no need for the money of those who harbor doubt.

As for the cause of the Occultation that has occurred, indeed Allah (Exalted and Mighty) says: 'O you who believe! Do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will upset you.' None of my forefathers was without having an oath of allegiance placed on his neck for the tyrant of his time. And when I emerge, I will emerge with no oath of allegiance to any tyrant on my neck.

As for the manner of benefiting from me during my Occultation, it is like benefiting from the sun when clouds hide it from sight. And I am the security for the people of the earth, just as the stars are the security for the people of the sky. So close the doors of asking about what does not concern you, and do not exert yourselves in what has been sufficient for you, and increase in supplication for the hastening of the Relief, for that is your relief.
Peace be upon you, O Ishaq ibn Yaqub, and upon those who follow the guidance.
ai.seo_question: What are the key theological and legal rulings in the Epistle of Imam al-Mahdi to Ishaq ibn Yaqub?
ai.summary: This seminal Tawqi' from Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) to Ishaq ibn Yaqub serves as a comprehensive manual for the Shia community during the Minor and Major Occultations, establishing the jurists (Rawat) as his proxy and clarifying the theological status of key figures like Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and Imam Husayn. It provides specific jurisprudential rulings on food, wealth, and the prohibition of doubting companions, while famously comparing the Imam's hidden presence to the sun behind clouds, thereby encouraging continuous spiritual reliance despite physical absence. The text also addresses the political reality of the 'bi'ah' (oath of allegiance) to contemporary rulers, distinguishing between obligatory submission and the Imam's own exemption, thus shaping the Shia model of political quietism and authority.
